diagnostic_evidence.quote: if the fluctuations \eqref{eq:fluctuation_definition} are constructed from an EC numerical flux $\mbf{f}^{\tt EC}:=\mbf{f}^{\tt EC}(\bB{u}^-,\bB{u}^+)$ that satisfies the entropy conservation condition

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed formula equals only the minus fluctuation of (eq:fluctuation_definition) with f* = f^EC, yet it is written with a \pm superscript defining both EC fluctuations. The correct plus fluctuation is (1/2)B(u^+)[[u]] + f(u^+) - f^EC, which differs in the sign of the flux difference. Read literally for the plus sign, D_EC^- + D_EC^+ = 2 f^EC - f(u^-) - f(u^+) + avg(B)[[u]], which violates the path-conservation condition (eq:path_conservation_cond) (which requires [[f]] plus the path integral) and destroys the interface identity w^-T D_EC^- + w^+T D_EC^+ = [[F]] on which the semi-discrete entropy conservation of the scheme rests.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define D_EC^+ (and hence D_ES^+) from (eq:fluctuation_definition) with f* = f^EC, i.e. D_EC^+(u^-,u^+) = (1/2)B(u^+)[[u]] + f(u^+) - f^EC(u^-,u^+), and restrict (eq:ec_fluctuation_definition) to the minus sign.
issues.overall_effect: The surface fluctuation applied at the left boundary of each element in (eq:dgsem)/(eq:es_dgsem) and reused in (eq:es_fluctuation_definition) is not correctly defined; a literal implementation yields a scheme that is neither path-conservative nor entropy conservative, so the EC/ES guarantees are unsupported until the definition is repaired.
issues.title: EC fluctuation definition assigns the minus-fluctuation formula to both signs, contradicting the general fluctuation definition and path conservation
issues.why_classification: A one-formula local correction, forced by (eq:fluctuation_definition), restores a consistent definition; with it all stated guarantees (entropy conservation/stability, well-balancedness) hold unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For the SWME entropy variables, w_1 = g(h+b) - u_m^2/2 - (1/2) sum alpha_i^2/(2i+1) contains moment terms, so the SWE bracket in (eq:entropy_conservation_condition_swe) equals -avg(hu_m) sum_j avg(alpha_j)[[alpha_j]]/(2j+1), nonzero whenever moments jump (the identity holds only when all moments vanish; e.g. for states (h,u_m,alpha_1,alpha_2) = (1,0,0,0) and (2,1,1,1) with b=0, g=1 it equals -4/15). The proof discards this bracket in (eq:leftside:EC:linearity). Moreover, contracting the moment flux component avg(hu_m)avg(alpha_j) of (eq:swme_ec_fluxes) with [[w_{j+2}]] = [[alpha_j]]/(2j+1) produces the additional term sum_j [[alpha_j]]avg(hu_m)avg(alpha_j)/(2j+1), which is omitted in the first equality of (eq:leftside:EC:P) (in the example the true bracket is 4/3, not the displayed 16/15 = [[P^LM]]). The two errors cancel exactly (the omitted term is +avg(hu_m) sum avg(alpha_j)[[alpha_j]]/(2j+1)), so the statement of thm:ec_flux is in fact true, but its proof establishes the conclusion through two false identities.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the hierarchical decomposition in the proof: retain the nonzero SWE bracket in (eq:leftside:EC:linearity) and include the omitted term sum_j [[alpha_j]]avg(hu_m)avg(alpha_j)/(2j+1) in (eq:leftside:EC:P), then verify the two contributions cancel so the total equals [[P^LM]] + [[Pbar^LM]] = [[w^T f - F]].
issues.overall_effect: The central entropy-conservation property of the flux f^EC (thm:ec_flux), on which the semi-discrete entropy conservation of the EC scheme and the entropy stability of the ES scheme rest, is left without a valid proof as written; no other labelled result uses the false identity.
issues.title: Proof of the entropy-conservative flux theorem invokes a false SWE identity and drops a compensating term
issues.why_classification: The proof of a central theorem fails at two compensating steps (a false premise and a dropped term); the repair needs a contained but nontrivial rederivation of the cancellation, although no claim, guarantee, or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: that for  constant bottom topography satisfies the relation $\text{diag}(\bar{\mbf{H}}, 1) \jump{\bB{w}} = \jump{\bB{u}}$

issues.failure_explanation: The exact inverse Hessian of E with respect to (h, hu_m, h alpha) is (1/g) y y^T + diag(0, h, 3h, ..., (2N+1)h) with y = (1, u_m, alpha)^T; correspondingly, for constant bottom the jump relation diag(Hbar,1)[[w]] = [[u]] requires the first diagonal entry of (1/g)diag(avg z) to be 0, since [[h]] = (1/g) avg(y)^T [[w]] already supplies the (1,1) contribution. With the stated z_1 = 1 one gets Hbar_11 = 2/g instead of 1/g: for two states with constant b, equal u_m and alpha but h^- != h^+ (so [[w]] = (g[[h]],0,...,0)), the relation yields 2[[h]] != [[h]]. Hbar is then also not the inverse Hessian at any state. The matrix remains positive definite, so the entropy-stability and well-balancedness arguments (which use only Hbar > 0 and the zero block for the b component) are unaffected.

failure_location.quote: with vectors $\mbf{y} = (1, u_m, \bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})^{\rm T}$ and $\mbf{z} = (1, gh, 3gh, \dots, (2n+1)gh)^{\rm T}$ is the positive definite inverse of the Hessian of the entropy function $\mathbb{E}\big((h, hu_m, h\bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})\big)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set the first component of z to 0, i.e. z = (0, gh, 3gh, ..., (2N+1)gh)^T (also correcting (2n+1) to (2N+1)); then diag(Hbar,1)[[w]] = [[u]] holds exactly for constant bottom and Hbar coincides with the inverse Hessian at the averaged-primitive state.
issues.overall_effect: The stated design properties of the ES dissipation (the exact relation diag(Hbar,1)[[w]] = [[u]] to conservative-variable jumps for constant bottom, and the inverse-Hessian/intermediate-state interpretation) are false as written, and the dissipation actually defined differs from the intended Rusanov-type dissipation by an extra 1/g in the (1,1) entry; no advertised guarantee of the ES scheme is lost.
issues.title: Wrong first component of z in the ES dissipation matrix Hbar falsifies the claimed jump relation and inverse-Hessian property
issues.why_classification: A single-entry local correction (z_1: 1 -> 0) restores both claimed properties; positive definiteness, entropy stability, and well-balancedness hold with either value, so no substantive guarantee depends on the erroneous entry.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the unscaled coefficients are $\widetilde{A}_{ijk}\coloneqq A_{ijk}/(2i+1)$ and $\widetilde{B}_{ijk} \coloneqq B_{ijk}/(2i+1)$

issues.failure_explanation: From (eq:condition) with the tilde definitions, A_{kji} = -((2k+1)/(2i+1)) B_{ijk} - B_{kji}; the displayed formula drops the factor (2k+1)/(2i+1) on B_{ijk} and is therefore false whenever i != k. Concretely, for the shifted Legendre basis B_{112} = 1/5 and B_{211} = -1, so the true value is A_{211} = 2/3, while the formula gives A_{211} = -(1/5 - 1) = 4/5. Computing the A tensor with this formula yields wrong coefficients, corrupting the mathfrak A_i terms, the physical and EC fluxes, and the identity (eq:condition) on which the entropy analysis relies.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by A_{kji} = -((2k+1)/(2i+1)) B_{ijk} - B_{kji} (equivalently, state the relation for the scaled coefficients: Atilde_{kji} = -(Btilde_{ijk} + Btilde_{kji})).
issues.overall_effect: The tensor-computation instruction of Appendix B, if implemented as written, produces an incorrect A_{ijk} tensor (for i != k), so the discretized system would not be the SWME and the entropy-conservative property of the flux would be lost; the paper's theoretical results are unaffected.
issues.title: Appendix B computes A_{kji} from B_{ijk} with a missing scaling factor
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction to the computational formula, forced by (eq:condition); no theorem, proof, or guarantee changes.
